learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected 0.2 units and locked it in.
observations.exploration: Ran from zero pH 1.0 to 24.90 mL pH 3.7; four drops reached 25.10 mL pH 10.3. Empty reset to zero. Repeated approach and added individual drops: 24.95 mL pH 4.0, 25.00 pH 7.0 and 25.05 pH 10.0.
observations.reveal: Corrected to 6 to 7 units, compared the 6.6 unit jump with the first 24.90 mL producing only 2.7 units, explained powers of ten and acid-base matching.
observations.visual: Actual dark 1257 by 936 screenshot inspected. Pink trace showed a nearly vertical cliff at 25 mL; numeric pH and volume, step controls and explanation were visible. Scientific notation rendered legibly.
observations.previewIsolation: Preview banner said history and analytics are not saved.
observations.blinding: No source, builder notes or other reviewers judgments inspected.

prediction.reason: A concrete numerical prediction is present but assumes unfamiliar chemical setup.
prediction.evidence: HCl, NaOH, mol/L and titrated appear before explanation.

interaction.reason: Coarse approach, fine drops and reset enable a genuine boundary test.

payoff.reason: Reveal connects the abrupt curve to matching acid and base.
payoff.evidence: 6.6 units over four drops versus 2.7 over previous 24.90 mL.

clarity.reason: Visual result is clear but novice vocabulary burden remains.
clarity.evidence: pH powers of ten explained only after chemical prediction.

transfer.reason: Titration usefulness and matching condition are explained without a new case.
transfer.evidence: Sharp matching point can locate equivalence.

accessibility.evidence: Textual pH and volume observed; screen reader, keyboard, contrast and reduced motion unaudited.

surprise.reason: A tiny addition changes the displayed pH dramatically.

visualExplanation.reason: Accumulated curve exposes the local cliff.

playfulness.reason: Drop controls and Empty support experimentation.

practicalValue.reason: Explains why an analytical measurement can locate a point sharply.

depth.reason: Combines logarithmic measurement and chemical balance.
depth.evidence: Residual acid concentration and excess base explanation.

complexity.reason: Simple button controls mask substantial chemistry and logarithm prerequisites.
complexity.conceptualDemand: Relate logarithmic pH to residual acid, excess base and equivalence.
complexity.interfaceBurden: One coarse approach, three increment buttons and reset.
complexity.prerequisiteNovelty: Acid/base names, concentration, titration and pH are not all introduced before prediction.
complexity.notationRepresentationBurden: Decimal millilitres, mol/L, H plus and scientific powers of ten.

whyCool: Fine drops turn a smooth-looking accumulation into a sharp chemical boundary.
caveat: The specified strong acid/base setup carries substantial assumed vocabulary for an everyday-numeracy learner.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
